A1.justification: Both PDFs describe GESC, and their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures and appendices support comparison. Retained material can be matched across relocation and renumbering; the omitted experimental appendix is a document change, not an extraction gap.

before.justification: V1 reports original node-classification results and ablations in Tables 1–2, plus large-graph, link-prediction and controlled experimental results in Appendix D.

after.justification: V2 retains original node-classification results, component ablations, hyperparameter sensitivity and depth experiments, including revised ablation values and an additional baseline.

M1.justification: The core transport, SIC, attention and training objective remain. V2 removes the residual-gate bias b_m from both the defining equation and Algorithm 1. It also changes modReLU's denominator from |z| plus epsilon only at zero to |z| plus epsilon everywhere (v1 Eq. 22; v2 Eq. 27). These are limited procedural revisions.

E1.justification: The nine main node-classification datasets remain, but v1's evaluations on Penn94, arXiv-year and snap-patents disappear. Link prediction on Cora, Citeseer, Pubmed and Squirrel is also removed. This substantially narrows the evaluated populations, graph scales and task coverage.

E2.justification: V2 adds L2DGCN to Table 1 while retaining its existing comparators. Removing v1 Tables 5 and 7 eliminates evaluated comparators such as VAGE, GCN†, DropEdge† and MSGNN, alongside component-substitution comparisons. The numerous methods in v2's new Table 3 are conceptual comparisons, not additional evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: The retained classification protocol still uses 20 training labels per class and an equal validation/test split. However, v2 removes the phase-perturbation procedure and its prediction-agreement, logit-deviation and attention-KL metrics, the attention-variant ROC-AUC evaluation, and the matched-parameter/compute substitution design. These are substantial removals of evaluation protocols, not demonstrated reruns of retained experiments.

E4.justification: V1 Appendix D.3–D.6 is removed: attention and gating variants, numerical gauge-invariance verification, SIC regularization/rank/placement ablations, and component cross-substitution studies. These tested distinct questions about phase handling and the source of gains. The main component ablation, SIC/JS sensitivity surfaces and depth analysis remain.

E5.justification: Both implementation appendices state ten random seeds and reporting of means and standard deviations. Neither version introduces a different uncertainty-estimation practice, confidence intervals or formal significance tests. Added and removed result entries do not change this reporting policy.

E6.justification: Existing Table 1 scores are unchanged, but new L2DGCN results exceed GESC on Actor (31.3 versus 30.4) and Texas (76.7 versus 74.5). Table 2's without-SIC scores change from 83.5 to 82.4 on Cora, 62.1 to 60.7 on Chameleon, and 71.2 to 68.2 on Texas. All results in v1 Tables 4–7 and Figures 5–6 are removed; the retained sensitivity and depth plots are unchanged.

T1.justification: The propositions, assumptions, proofs and heuristic spectral discussion remain substantively unchanged, with Appendix B becoming Appendix C. Limited mathematical-definition changes include the revised modReLU denominator and removal of the alternative attention-logit definitions in v1 Eqs. 114–115. No new theoretical guarantee or corrected proof is supplied.

C1.justification: The principal SIC, sign-aware gating, gauge transport and performance contributions remain. The abstract adds a stronger scientific assertion: absent interference handling in existing gauge-based GNNs is a primary driver of oversmoothing under gauge transport. V1 primarily contrasted architectural mechanisms without making this explicit causal diagnosis.

C2.justification: V2 adds specific limitations concerning complex-valued computation, sensitivity to nonlinearities, extension beyond U(1), and extreme graph noise. New Appendix A substantially expands explanations connecting earlier model families' weaknesses to missing interference control. Conversely, v1's interpretations of large-graph generalization, link prediction, phase coupling, projector choices and cross-substitution evidence disappear.

D1.justification: The code pointer changes from an anonymous 4open.science address to a named GitHub repository. V2 removes the alternative node-wise precomputation discussion from v1 Appendix A.3 and the shared/diagonal parameterization details from D.3. Core PyTorch Geometric, optimizer, hardware and early-stopping disclosures remain; relocation alone is not a reproducibility change.

R1.justification: New Appendix A and Table 3 substantially expand positioning across homophily, heterophily, spectral, diffusion, sheaf, magnetic and gauge networks. Added citations include L2DGCN, GraphSAGE, JKNet, sheaf methods and lattice gauge-equivariant CNNs, supporting an explicit first-combination claim. The variational graph-autoencoder reference disappears with the link-prediction comparison.

P1.justification: Most retained prose and the main section sequence remain stable, with edits to the abstract and selected paragraphs. Scalability moves into Section 4.3; the new comparative appendix shifts appendix lettering, and the experimental appendix is deleted. Limitations and acknowledgements are added, while authorship, correspondence and publication-header text change. Extensive rewriting of the retained exposition is not evident.

P2.justification: V1's introductory illustration, experimental Figures 5–6 and Tables 4–7 are removed. V2 adds the large model-family comparison table, expands Table 1 with L2DGCN, and updates and relocates the architecture diagram. The sensitivity and depth images remain identical despite renumbering, and the dataset-statistics table is retained as Table 4.

improvement.justification: The L2DGCN comparison, expanded positioning and explicit limitations are useful additions. However, removing the gauge-verification, projector and cross-substitution studies eliminates direct evidence supporting the central mechanisms and attribution of gains; large-graph and link-prediction evidence also disappears. Meanwhile, the abstract strengthens its causal claim about oversmoothing without corresponding new analysis. This substantial loss of empirical support outweighs the contextual improvements.
